description.narrative:
Building on the lessons learnt, success and impact of the first phase of the project between November 2019 to August 2022 and aiming to keep working in synergy with the USA and Swiss under MSDA project, Internews proposes the Reinforcing Rural Radios in DRC (3R-DRC) project with the aim of continuing under the same framework, with slightly refined objectives, for a period of 36 months. Having noted the information dynamics in the country and in rural areas as well as the need for holistic support, the second phase of the project will focus more on remote, underserved locations where audience reach is still a problem and where the marginalisation of women and youth is more acute. The second phase aims to broaden and scale up the impacts and achievements from the first phase to sustain partners’ capacity and actions and secure more long-term effects in a conducive context where the government appears to exhibit political will in adopting reforms and addressing governance issues.
The 3R-DRC project will focus on the following provinces where Internews and local partners have established strong presence, networks and activities (Most of the provinces were covered during the first phase of the programme): Kongo Central, Sud Kivu, Kasai, Kasai Central, Kasai Oriental, Haut Katanga, Lualaba, Tshopo, Haut Uele, Bas Uele, Equateur and Kinshasa.

Med utgångspunkt i erfarenheterna, framgångarna och effekterna av projektets första fas mellan november 2019 och augusti 2022 och i syfte att fortsätta att arbeta i synergi med USA och Schweiz inom ramen för MSDA-projektet föreslår Internews projektet Reinforcing Rural Radios in DRC (3R-DRC) i syfte att fortsätta inom samma ram, med något mer detaljerade mål, under en period på 36 månader. Efter att ha noterat informationsdynamiken i landet och på landsbygden samt behovet av holistiskt stöd kommer projektets andra fas att inriktas mer på avlägsna och underförsörjda platser där det fortfarande är svårt att nå ut till publiken och där marginaliseringen av kvinnor och ungdomar är mer akut. Syftet med den andra fasen är att bredda och skala upp effekterna och resultaten från den första fasen för att stödja partnernas kapacitet och åtgärder och säkra mer långsiktiga effekter i ett gynnsamt sammanhang där regeringen verkar visa politisk vilja att anta reformer och ta itu med frågor som rör styrelseformer.
3R-DRC-projektet kommer att fokusera på följande provinser där Internews och lokala partner har etablerat stark närvaro, nätverk och verksamhet (de flesta av provinserna täcktes under programmets första fas): Kongo Central, Sud Kivu, Kasai, Kasai Central, Kasai Oriental, Haut Katanga, Lualaba, Tshopo, Haut Uele, Bas Uele, Equateur och Kinshasa.

The overall objective of this intervention is to promote a more open and vibrant community radio sector that meets the information needs of citizens in rural areas (with a focus on women and youth) and strengthens their participation in public debate.
Internews and its local partners will achieve this through the following intermediate results:
1. Improve the legal framework and the capacity to protect journalists for rural community radios with media reforms and safeguarding mechanisms
2. Improve the business and financial sustainability of rural radio stations
3. Increase the quantity, quality and reach of rural radio content on democracy and human rights, electoral education and SGBV.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
The objectives of the Strengthening Rural Radios in RDC is to support rural radios by improving their economic viability , content quality and legal environment running from July 2022 to June 2025 (36 months) with a total budget of USD 4,71 million , the project has been implemented in a context marked by persistent political tensions and significant economic challenges.
The final evaluation finds that the project has been highly relevant to the needs of rural community radios, particularly on journalistic skills and producing content tailored to local expectations. Notably 78 % of women and 80 % of young people reported that the content broadcast responded to their needs. The enhancement of a new press law in March 2023 represent a significant step forward in the official recognition of community radios.
The average revenue of radio stations rose from USD 15 USD quarterly to 102 USD one year after. 94 % of media professionals interviewed thought that the project had brought positive change, particularly by strengthening radio governance, improving quality of content, and inclusion of women and in public debate.
The final evaluation also highlight remaining challenges such as the lack of technical equipment and insufficient legal protection mechanisms for journalists. The evaluation recommends strengthening economic and technical training for radio staff, promoting digital innovation and rising community awareness about the role of local radio. In the medium term it advises radio stations to develop more inclusive programs address critical issues such as civic education, governance, culture and sustainable development and co create content with the citizens.
The evaluation also states that the project was relevant and led up to concrete results and significant progress in the media sector in DRC. It has improved the quality of information, fostered more inclusive journalistic practices and supported the empowerment of local actors. To sustain these results, continued efforts in financing, regulatory support and digital innovation are essential to ensure a pluralistic free and resilient media environment.
The efficiency is assessed to be very good in general also with regards to budget efficiency, media production and training capacity. The impact is also assessed to be high and the probability that the benefits from the project last is also assessed as high by the evaluation.
